review_evidence: README describes the package as Hax’s Lean proof library containing extracted models of Rust core/std/alloc plus verification tactics.

The source includes formal CoreModels for Rust libraries and Hoare/WP infrastructure, with theorems such as Result.ok_spec, Result.fail_spec, Result.deterministic and Triple composition/entailment lemmas.
These definitions and specification lemmas are part of a program-verification semantics/model library, not merely an editor/build tool, and are useful formal-methods prior art.
summary: Reviewed hax-lean; retain its formal models and verification infrastructure for extracted Rust code.

review_evidence: Ran the declaration-keyword grep across all 33 listed files: thirteen matched zero, two matched exactly one, the remaining eighteen matched between 4 and 1578.

Read all thirteen zero-match files in full: each is a short list of `import` lines, most with a module-level `/-! ... -/` doc comment, no declaration, open, notation, or executable command in any of them.

Read CoreModels/MissingAeneas.lean in full: its one grep hit is the word 'theorem' inside a docstring code example illustrating usage; the file's actual content is a `scoped syntax` and `macro_rules` definition for a `%ToLowerCase` elaboration helper inside `namespace Aeneas.Std.ScalarElab`.
Read Tests/Hax/Tactic/ForLoopWithInvariantSpec.lean in full: a genuine `example` with a full tactic-mode proof of a for-loop invariant specification under `namespace Hax.Tests`.

Confirmed the largest file, CoreModels/Core/Funs.lean (696329 bytes), has 1578 declaration-keyword matches, consistent with it being the bulk auto-extracted Lean model of Rust's `core` crate that the prior review already characterized as the source's formal model content.

Spot-checked CoreModels/RustPrimitives/Funs.lean (48508 bytes, 271 declarations) and CoreModels/Core/Types.lean (45898 bytes, 160 declarations), confirming genuine extracted/verification content rather than stubs.

summary: Reviewed all 54 changed/added files in the cryspen__hax-lean repository. The unit contains two categories of files: (1) 13 pure import aggregators that only re-export other modules with documentation comments and @[expose] attributes (CoreModels.lean, CoreModels/Core.lean, CoreModels/Alloc.lean, CoreModels/Command.lean, CoreModels/Spec.lean, CoreModels/HaxLib.lean, CoreModels/RustPrimitives.lean, Hax.lean, Tests.lean, Tests/Hax.lean, Tests/Hax/Tactic.lean, Hax/MissingLean.lean, Hax/Tactic.lean), and (2) 41 files with substantial formal mathematical content including 100+ inductive type/structure declarations (CoreModels/Core/Types.lean, CoreModels/Alloc/Types.lean, CoreModels/Core/TypesPrologue.lean, CoreModels/RustPrimitives/Types.lean), 1500+ function/trait implementations with @spec annotations (CoreModels/Core/Funs.lean, CoreModels/Core/FunsEpilogue.lean, CoreModels/Core/FunsPrologue.lean, CoreModels/Alloc/Funs.lean, CoreModels/RustPrimitives/Funs.lean, CoreModels/HaxLib/Int.lean, CoreModels/HaxLib/Prop.lean), verification condition specs with proofs (CoreModels/Spec/RustPrimitives/Arithmetic.lean, CoreModels/Spec/RustPrimitives/Slice.lean), custom tactic implementations with meta-programming (CoreModels/Command/OpenHidingNamespace.lean, Hax/Tactic/*.lean), missing infrastructure lemmas (CoreModels/MissingAeneas.lean, Hax/MissingAeneas.lean, Hax/MissingLean/Std/Do/Triple/Basic.lean), and test files with executable proofs (Tests/Hax/Tactic/*.lean). Per FILTER-007, import aggregators are navigation data but should be ranked not filtered; they contain @[expose] attributes and documentation comments that are searchable auxiliary metadata. Per FILTER-004 and FILTER-021, no content-level reason exists to hard-exclude any file — all contain either formal mathematical declarations/proofs or navigation-relevant module structure. Per FILTER-022, the appropriate disposition is to retain all files.
